newsitem.title: USA: Anti-tobacco U.S. senators skeptical on settlement.
newsitem.headline: Anti-tobacco U.S. senators skeptical on settlement.

text.p: Three senators who have actively pushed for controls on tobacco said Wednesday they were highly skeptical of the reported negotiations on a potential settlement of claims against tobacco manufacturers.

Sens. Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, Richard Durbin of Illinois and Ron Wyden of Oregon, all Democrats, said they expressed their reservations in a letter to President Clinton. The letter will be released at a news conference held by the three senators at 12:45 p.m. EDT (1645 GMT).
Separately, a congressional aide to an anti-tobacco lawmaker said there was a mixed reaction among congressional opponents of the tobacco industry to the reported settlement negotiations.
"Millions of people have had their loved ones die as a result of tobacco. Millions of people have had their health harmed. We have to make sure we don't sell them out," he said.

"Whatever happens, the interests of the people who have been harmed have to be protected. What happens to the people who have real claims against the tobacco companies? Will they be adequately taken care of?"

While they were heartened by tobacco companies willingness to submit to Food and Drug Administration jurisdiction and to list chemical ingredients on tobacco packages, the source said they were concerned about just how far tobacco companies would go towards fulfiling these commitments.
